title: Components of Creative Arts and Sports
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Creative Arts and Sports; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts and Sports teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Draw the grand stave on the board; notes are named in words on the phone. Fitness drills on the field with music.

skills.key_step: The child names the elements of a play: plot, characters, setting, theme, conflict, resolution, dialogue and stage directions.

floor.prerequisite: Names the elements of a story (Grade 7).
floor.question: What is the setting of a story?

steps: Read or watch a short scene.
contexts: a class play on a social issue

board.do: They agree to share. Which element?

misconceptions.ask: What is conflict in a play?
misconceptions.repair: Find the conflict in a play with no fighting at all.

misconceptions.ask: Where does the resolution come in a play?
misconceptions.repair: Order the parts of a known play: introduction, conflict, climax, resolution.

misconceptions.ask: What is the theme of a play?
misconceptions.repair: Ask "what is the play teaching?" after retelling.

misconceptions.ask: Are stage directions spoken aloud in a performance?
misconceptions.repair: Act out "(she opens the door slowly)" without saying it.

checks.question: What is the resolution of a play?
checks.answer: the part where the conflict is settled

skills.key_step: The child tells power (strength used quickly) and reaction time (quick response to a signal) from the other components and names activities that train them.
representations: a ruler for the drop test
steps: Respond to a signal: reaction time.
Choose the activity that trains it.

misconceptions.ask: What is the difference between strength and power?
misconceptions.repair: Compare lifting a bag slowly (strength) and a vertical jump (power).

misconceptions.ask: What is reaction time?
misconceptions.repair: Do the ruler-drop test: catch it as fast as you can.

misconceptions.ask: Which activity trains power?
misconceptions.repair: Match each activity to what it trains.

misconceptions.ask: A sprinter practises starts to the gun. What does this train?
misconceptions.repair: Practise starts to a clap and time the response.

checks.question: Which activity trains reaction time?
checks.answer: any of: starts to a signal, the ruler-drop catch

skills.key_step: The child names pitches on the grand stave: treble and bass joined by a brace, middle C on the ledger line between them.

floor.question: What are the bass staff spaces?

representations: a grand stave on the board
steps: Middle C sits between the staves.
contexts: reading a piano or choir score
a school song in four parts

board.do: Point at the ledger line between the staves.

misconceptions.ask: Is middle C on the treble staff the same note as middle C on the bass staff?
misconceptions.repair: Play middle C and show both ways of writing it.

misconceptions.ask: What is the note on the bottom line of the bass staff?
misconceptions.repair: Check the clef before naming any note.

misconceptions.ask: What does the brace on a grand stave show?
misconceptions.repair: Show piano music: both hands read at once.

misconceptions.ask: Which staff of the grand stave holds the low notes?
misconceptions.repair: Sing low and point to the bass staff.

checks.question: Where is middle C on the grand stave?
checks.answer: on a ledger line between the treble and bass staves

skills.key_step: The child groups notes in four-four time with dots and ties: four beats per bar, a dot adds half, a tie joins same-pitch notes.

floor.question: How many beats is a dotted minim?

steps: Draw the bar line at four.

board.do: A dotted crotchet and a quaver make how many beats?

misconceptions.ask: How many beats is a dotted crotchet?
misconceptions.repair: A crotchet is 1; half of 1 is a half; 1 + a half = one and a half.

misconceptions.ask: Can a tie join a C and a D?
misconceptions.repair: Show a tie (same pitch, held) and a slur (different pitches, smooth).

misconceptions.ask: A bar has a dotted minim and a minim. Is it a correct bar of four-four?
misconceptions.repair: Write the beat count under each note.

misconceptions.ask: Which beats are strong in four-four time?
misconceptions.repair: Count ONE two THREE four while stepping.

checks.question: How many beats is a dotted crotchet?
What does a tie join?
checks.answer: two notes of the same pitch

skills.key_step: The child builds F major: F G A B-flat C D E F, one flat (B flat) on every B, home note F.

floor.question: Which note is sharp in G major?

steps: Write the next seven notes in order.

board.do: Write F G A B C D E F.

misconceptions.ask: F major has one...
misconceptions.repair: Write F G A B C D E F and play it: B must be lowered.

misconceptions.ask: Which note is flat in F major?
misconceptions.repair: Count the steps from F: the fourth note, B, is lowered.

misconceptions.ask: On which note does F major start and end?
misconceptions.repair: The key name is the home note.

misconceptions.ask: In F major, is every B played as B flat?
misconceptions.repair: Circle every B in an F major tune.

checks.question: Which note is flat in F major?
On which note does F major start and end?
